post.text:
Your support team is 70% busywork.

I watched a consultancy lose money on every retainer they sold.
Not because clients were hard. Because L1 tickets ate the margin.

3 things that fixed it:

1. Classify before you reply. Half the tickets are status checks.
2. Let AI resolve the boring 70%. Humans take the 30% that needs judgement.
3. Measure cost per resolved ticket, not tickets per agent.

What % of your tickets could a bot close today?

(Building this at TixA — DM me if you want the checklist.)

self_comments: The number that surprised me: 'where is my order' was 38% of volume. Nobody had measured it.
Curious — does your team track cost per resolved ticket? Most don't.

carousel.title: 70% of support tickets don't need a human
carousel.subtitle: The 5-step audit we run before any AI goes live
carousel.cta: Save this. Run the audit Monday.

slides.title: Export 30 days of tickets
slides.body: Subject + first message is enough. Don't boil the ocean.

slides.title: Tag the top 10 intents
slides.body: Order status, returns, warranty, password, invoice. You'll cover 80% with ten.

slides.title: Mark what needs judgement
slides.body: Refund exceptions, angry VIPs, legal. That's your human 30%.

slides.title: Price a human reply
slides.body: Loaded cost ÷ tickets per hour. Most teams land at $4–9 per ticket.

slides.title: Automate only the boring 70%
slides.body: Ship one intent at a time. Measure resolution rate weekly.

engagement_comments.comment:
The adoption gap isn't tooling, it's permission.
Teams we work with ship 3x faster once a VP says 'you won't be blamed for trying'.
Who owns that permission in most orgs?
